title: Large Language Models
summary: Making computation in large language models more efficient, stable, and deployable — not just larger.
argument: Most computation in a forward pass does not improve model output. Parameters activate that contribute nothing. Training runs produce instabilities that waste days of compute. Inference pipelines hit throughput limits that were predictable but unaddressed.

This program treats efficiency, stability, and deployability as engineering problems with measurable causes. We study how models allocate computation, how training dynamics behave at scale, and how inference systems handle real operating conditions.
currentWork: Reviewing routing objective designs and running small-scale MoE experiments to measure the interaction between load-balancing loss terms and training stability.
futureDirection: Co-optimizing routing and sparsity decisions during training to reduce instability from simultaneous tuning.
